notes: A Hebrew relative is present, so rule 46's first rider gives אֲשֶׁר both 'whom' and the supplied antecedent 'they', with the head on the relative itself.
The verbless clause's 'are' joins the predicate phrase's own unit (that same אֲשֶׁר unit) rather than the past-tense 'set' inside the relative clause.
בֵּית יְהוָה is an adverbial accusative, so the supplied 'in' is licensed by the noun's case-function (rule 33) and is not added.
'had rest' places the recasting's light verb with the noun carrying the lexeme, headed on 'rest' (rules 43-44).
